chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who endows a property (waqf), then it occurs to him to make a change in it. He said: 'If he endowed it for his children and others, then appointed a guardian for it, he may not revert to it, even if they are minors, and he had stipulated guardianship for them until they reach maturity and take possession for themselves. If they are adults and he has not handed it over to them, nor have they disputed it to take possession from him, then he may revert to it, because they do not take possession and they have reached maturity.'

key_terms.الضَّيْعَة: Property or estate (specifically in the context of waqf)

ai.seo_question: Can a person reclaim their endowed property (waqf) if the beneficiaries are adults but haven't taken possession?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), clarifying that the founder's right of reversion (ruju') depends on whether the beneficiaries have effectively taken possession (huz) of the waqf. The Imam distinguishes between minors, whose guardianship is retained by the founder until maturity, and adults, where the founder retains control only until they actually assume possession, highlighting the Shia juristic emphasis on actual possession over mere legal entitlement in waqf structures.
